SAP Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) Consultant (ICT Business Analyst – ANZSCO 261111)
Blu Pantera Tech Pty Ltd
Fortitude Valley, Brisbane QLD 4006
Full time
$140,000 – $180,000 per year + superannuation

About position
The SAP Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) Consultant is responsible for analysing business requirements, and designing, configuring and implementing SAP EAM solutions that optimise asset management and maintenance processes for clients operating in asset-intensive industries. The role partners with business stakeholders to maximise asset reliability, reduce maintenance costs and support digital transformation through effective SAP EAM solutions, while ensuring project delivery meets quality standards, timelines and client requirements.

Responsibilities
- Consult with clients, users and stakeholders to understand organisational objectives, operational requirements and asset management needs.
- Identify, investigate and analyse business processes, procedures and work practices to determine inefficiencies and opportunities for improvement.
- Define, document and validate functional requirements for SAP solutions supporting asset management and maintenance operations, and recommend process improvements and system enhancements.
- Design, configure and implement SAP Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) solutions aligned with operational requirements and industry best practice, including asset structures, functional locations, equipment records, maintenance notifications, work orders, preventive and corrective maintenance processes, maintenance plans and maintenance strategies.
- Develop functional specifications, data and process models, system documentation and process maps to support SAP solution design, configuration and development.
- Collaborate with technical consultants, developers and project teams to deliver integrated SAP solutions that meet business requirements and technical standards.
- Apply project management methodologies, principles and techniques to develop project plans, estimate costs, allocate resources and manage SAP EAM implementation activities to achieve project milestones and deadlines.
- Develop and execute test plans, including unit, integration and user acceptance testing (UAT), and coordinate data migration, master data validation, system deployment and go-live activities.
- Prepare user documentation, business process documentation and training materials, and deliver formal training to end users.
- Provide post-implementation support, troubleshoot functional issues and monitor SAP EAM processes and performance to identify improvements.
- Act as a central functional reference point throughout project delivery, liaising with clients, users, project managers, developers and cross-functional teams to ensure solutions meet requirements, quality standards and project objectives.

Skills and Qualifications required to perform the above job role
- Tertiary qualification in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Information Systems or a related discipline. 
- SAP certification or relevant SAP EAM/PM training is highly regarded.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience implementing and supporting SAP Enterprise Asset Management (SAP EAM/PM) solutions.
- Strong business analysis skills, with the ability to identify business requirements, analyse processes and develop functional specifications, process models, documentation and test plans.
- Experience in project management, with strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills, and the ability to oversee the implementation of complex IT projects.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage with technical teams, business stakeholders and end users.

## Cyber Security Advice and Assessment Specialist
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Cyber Security Advice and Assessment Specialist to join our team and play a pivotal role in safeguarding our organisation's information assets and digital infrastructure. This position is responsible for conducting security assessments, interpreting policies, and delivering expert guidance on cyber security strategies and risk management. The ideal candidate brings a strong technical foundation combined with the ability to communicate complex security concepts to a broad range of stakeholders. This role suits a proactive professional who thrives in dynamic environments and is committed to continuously strengthening an organisation's security posture.
## Key Responsibilities
- Conduct comprehensive risk assessments and security control evaluations to identify vulnerabilities and weaknesses across the organisation's systems, networks, and cyber security policies
- Perform vulnerability testing and threat analysis, translating findings into actionable recommendations that reduce exposure and strengthen overall defences
- Provide specialist advice and practical guidance on security strategies, helping stakeholders understand and effectively manage identified risks and emerging threats
- Develop, implement, and maintain security policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines that support a robust and consistent organisational security posture
- Lead and support investigations into security incidents, producing clear and thorough reports on findings and guiding the refinement of detection and response processes
- Assist with root cause analysis following security incidents or breaches, assessing the extent of impact and recommending appropriate remedial and preventative actions
- Review and assess information system designs to ensure security requirements are embedded throughout development and implementation lifecycles
- Develop and maintain meaningful metrics and reporting frameworks that articulate the impact of cyber security risks on business processes and information assets
- Align and coordinate internal and external audit activities, security assessments, and compliance engagements to ensure consistent and efficient outcomes
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to embed security best practices across business operations and technology initiatives
- Communicate complex security concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, providing guidance that enables informed decision-making at all levels of the organisation
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline
- Demonstrated experience in a cyber security role with a focus on risk assessment, security advisory, or security operations
- Strong working knowledge of security frameworks and standards such as ISO 27001, NIST, ASD Essential Eight, or equivalent
- Proven ability to conduct vulnerability assessments, penetration testing coordination, and security control reviews
- Experience developing and implementing security policies, standards, and procedures within a complex organisational environment
- Solid understanding of network security, cloud security principles, identity and access management, and secure system design
- Experience investigating and reporting on security incidents, including root cause analysis and post-incident remediation
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess risk and prioritise effectively
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce clear reports and present findings to diverse audiences
- Familiarity with audit coordination and compliance assessment processes across regulatory or industry frameworks
- Ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
## Preferred Qualifications
- Relevant industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CompTIA Security+, or CEH
- Experience working within Australian Government security frameworks or with protective security requirements
- Familiarity with the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) guidelines and the Information Security Manual (ISM)
- Postgraduate qualifications in Cyber Security, Risk Management, or a related field
- Experience with security information and event management (SIEM) platforms or other security tooling
- Prior exposure to governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms or tools
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team that values innovation, continuous learning, and genuine contribution to meaningful security outcomes
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications and training programmes
- Enjoy a flexible working environment that supports work-life balance through hybrid arrangements and adaptable scheduling
- Contribute to high-impact work that directly protects critical systems and supports the organisation's strategic objectives
- Competitive remuneration package with clear pathways for career growth and advancement within the cyber security function
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

Concrete Support Services (CSS) is a fully independent concrete testing and engineering consultancy supporting construction projects right across Melbourne. From our laboratory and field operations, we deliver concrete testing, materials assessment and technical advice that builders, contractors and engineers rely on to keep their projects moving and compliant. Because we operate as a completely independent laboratory, our clients know that every result we issue is backed by integrity, confidentiality and impartiality. Our work aligns with Australian Standards and NATA requirements, and our team combines decades of hands-on concrete technology expertise with a genuine commitment to service. What sets us apart is speed paired with accuracy we understand that critical site activities can’t wait, so we go out of our way to turn around reliable field and laboratory results promptly and to consistently exceed what our clients expect. As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Technician to join our team at Oakleigh South and play a hands-on role in delivering the quality and responsiveness our clients count on.

Key Responsibilities
•	Carry out and coordinate a full program of on-site and in-laboratory tests on concrete, construction materials and soils including sampling fresh concrete, casting and curing specimens, slump and compressive strength testing all in accordance with Australian Standards.
•	Interpret job briefs, project specifications and work assignment instructions, then apply the appropriate testing procedures and select the correct equipment for each task.
•	Record, collate and analyse test results, perform the associated computations, and enter data accurately and promptly into our laboratory data-management systems so clients receive fast, dependable results.
•	Prepare technical sketches, charts, tabulations and test reports that support civil engineering works such as roads, drainage, water supply and sewerage reticulation systems, dams and structural elements where concrete and materials testing is required.
•	Conduct site inspections of concrete and civil works, and help organise and oversee sampling, re-testing and remedial or maintenance verification where required.
•	Estimate material quantities and associated costs, and check that materials and finished works comply with specifications, regulations and relevant contract provisions.
•	Collect field data during site surveys and sampling runs including on road, pavement and infrastructure projects and consolidate it for analysis and reporting.
•	Calibrate, maintain and correctly operate field and laboratory testing equipment, and keep clear records of its condition and use.
•	Uphold the laboratory’s quality management system and safeguard the integrity, impartiality and confidentiality of every result, in line with NATA and Australian Standards requirements.
•	Liaise professionally with clients, site supervisors and project engineers, providing clear technical support and rapid feedback to accommodate critical site timelines.
•	Support concrete mix design and quality-control activities, contributing observations and data that help clients meet their construction project needs.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety procedures and contribute to a safe, well-organised working environment both on site and in the laboratory.

About You
•	Strong attention to detail and a methodical, accurate approach to testing and record-keeping.
•	Reliable, punctual and able to manage priorities to meet time-critical site demands.
•	A team player who communicates clearly and professionally with colleagues and clients.
•	Committed to integrity, impartiality and confidentiality in all aspects of the work.
•	Safety-conscious, with a genuine respect for standards, procedures and compliance.
•	Physically capable of the practical, hands-on aspects of field and laboratory testing.
•	Willing to learn, take direction and grow within a supportive, quality-driven team.

Qualifications & Experience
•	An AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant civil, engineering or materials-related discipline.
•	At least 1 year of relevant experience.

What We Offer
•	Salary:  $75,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation per annum.
•	Hours: Full-time position, typically 38 hours per week.
•	Location: Oakleigh South, VIC.

How to Apply
If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume together with a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and qualifications.
